subject: AcmeCorp private offer — buyer onboarding, term options, and approval sequencing
messages:
From: Joe Sloan <joe.sloan@acmecorp.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: AcmeCorp Procurement <procure@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private offer options for Acme — term & buyer approvals

Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking this. We're evaluating Redwood for a cross-division deployment (Three business units: Commerce, Logistics, and Analytics). Procurement asked me to confirm a few things so we can decide whether to go through AWS Marketplace private offer or handle via a direct contract:

- Term options: Does Redwood support both 12-month and 36-month private offer commitments via the Marketplace? Any standard discount tiers for longer tenors?
- Buyer approvals: Our legal/procurement team requires that each BU's purchasing admin can approve the PO independently (we want separate buyer identities but a single consolidated invoice). Is that supported in the private-offer flow?
- Signature windows & PO flow: typical lead times to have an offer go live on the AWS side (we'll need the timelines to plan internal approvals).
- Any specific procurement docs you need from us up front? (We have an RFP — attaching for context.)

Attached: Acme_RFP_Q1.pdf

Can we schedule 30 minutes tomorrow to walk the options? Prefer mornings PST.

Thanks,
Joe Sloan
Senior Sourcing Manager — AcmeCorp
procure@acmecorp.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Joe Sloan <joe.sloan@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private offer options for Acme — term & buyer approvals

Hi Joe — thanks for the RFP and context. Quick answers up front, then a proposed next step.

Summary (short):
- Yes: we support 12- and 36-month private offers through AWS Marketplace. 36-month commitments commonly have a stepped discount schedule; we can propose a 10–18% discount range depending on consolidated spend and whether you want per-division metering.
- Buyer approvals: AWS private offers can be configured so each buyer identity (email) accepts the private offer; invoice consolidation is possible if you want Redwood to bill centrally and route cost back to divisions internally (we usually do this via consolidated billing options and an internal chargeback matrix).
- Timeline: once we submit the private offer to AWS, typical time-to-live is 1–5 business days provided buyer identities are verified and legal terms are standard. Longer if legal redlines or custom billing arrangements are needed.

Recommended next steps:
- You provide expected monthly/annual spend per BU and the canonical buyer emails for each BU.
- We propose two offer variants (12m @ standard list, 36m with stepped discount and a 30% overage cap).
- Redwood marketplace ops (Vanessa) will run an approval checklist and submit the private offer to AWS.

Attachments: redwood_private_offer_template_v2.pdf; buyer_approval_matrix.xlsx (sample)

Can we do 30 minutes tomorrow at 10:30am PST? If that works, I'll invite.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Account Executive — Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Joe Sloan <joe.sloan@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Feb 2028 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private offer options for Acme — term & buyer approvals

Priya / Joe — adding pricing context from the deals desk side.

Ben's quick take:
- If Acme consolidates purchase across all three BUs and commits to a 36-month term, we can increase the upper discount band to 15% (from 10%) on committed spend. That requires a single committed quantity on the PO (we'll handle internal allocation via billing tags).
- For separate per-BU acceptance (three buyers), we need to ensure each buyer email is whitelisted in the private offer; that's a simple entry during the AWS PO submission, but it does lengthen the verification step.
- Approval gating: any discount >12% will require a pricing exception sign-off from Sales Lead + Finance (we've pre-approved in-principle; just need formal sign-off once spend numbers are in).

Joe — can you confirm approximate committed ARR per BU? That will let us draft the two variants and run pricing exception if needed.

--

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Joe Sloan <joe.sloan@acmecorp.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, AWS Marketplace Seller Support <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Feb 2028 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private offer options for Acme — operational checklist and next actions

Hi all — operational notes from marketplace ops (cc'ing AWS support for visibility on buyer verification step).

Checklist & guidance:
1) Buyer identities: please send the canonical acceptance emails for each BU. They must be the emails that will accept the private offer in AWS (personal inboxes are fine but company-controlled emails are preferred). We will add them to the private offer whitelist.
2) Invoicing model: confirm whether you want Redwood to issue a single consolidated invoice (recommended) or separate invoices per BU. If consolidated, confirm the invoice remit and PO number structure.
3) Signature window: we recommend a 7-calendar-day acceptance window on the AWS private offer to avoid stale tokens; if procurement needs more time we can extend but that increases risk of price changes.
4) DocuSign / legal redlines: if Acme requires non-standard terms (data residency, custom indemnities), please flag now. Standard Redwood T&Cs are marketplace-friendly and usually do not require changes, which keeps the offer timeline at 1–3 business days.
5) AWS steps: once Redwood submits the private offer, AWS verifies buyer emails and places the offer in the buyer's account for acceptance. AWS support (cc'd) — please confirm typical verification SLA for whitelisted buyer emails.

Attachments: aws_po_checklist.md (checklist)

Action items:
- Joe: send buyer emails and preferred invoicing model (Consolidated / Per-BU + sample PO format).
- Priya / Ben: we'll prepare the two private-offer drafts and pricing exception doc (if we go >12% discount).

If everyone agrees, I will submit the private offer draft to AWS on Monday morning.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Marketplace Operations Lead — Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

From: Joe Sloan <joe.sloan@acmecorp.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: AcmeCorp Procurement <procure@acmecorp.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Feb 2028 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private offer options for Acme — buyer onboarding, term options, and approval sequencing

Priya / Vanessa / Ben — thanks for the clarity. We want to proceed with the Marketplace private offer. Details below: 

- Committed ARR by BU (estimated):
  - Commerce: $1,200,000 / year
  - Logistics: $650,000 / year
  - Analytics: $400,000 / year
- Buyer emails to whitelist (will accept the private offer):
  - commerce-purchasing@acmecorp.com
  - logistics-purchasing@acmecorp.com
  - analytics-purchasing@acmecorp.com
- Invoicing: Consolidated invoice to AcmeCorp AP (remit: ap@acmecorp.com). Will provide PO number per division to support internal chargebacks.

Attached: Acme_PO_Info.xlsx (contains PO number prefixes and AP contact info).

Request: Please confirm (1) that you can submit a 36-month private offer with the proposed consolidated billing model and (2) approximate timeline for the offer to be visible to our buyers and for DocuSign to trigger. We'd like the private offer live by Feb 28 at the latest.

Regards,
Joe Sloan
Senior Sourcing Manager — AcmeCorp
procure@acmecorp.com
